title: Real embeddings
subtitle: When "days off" finds "vacation" with no shared words
mission: Compare employee requests with HR questions. First by shared words (simulated), then with a real embedding model running on your device.

predict.question: "I want to take a few days off": which HR question is it closest to, for a real embedding model?

feedback.right: good. In simulated mode (shared words) nothing matches, because "days off" and "vacation" are different words. Pick "In the browser" and run again: the real model connects them by meaning.
feedback.wrong: a word search (simulated mode) indeed finds nothing. But an embedding model compares meaning: pick "In the browser" and see "vacation" on top.
feedback.skipped: no guess? Simulated mode only sees shared words. Pick "In the browser" to see meaning at work.

coach.ui: guess noted. Run in simulated mode, then pick "In the browser" (~120 MB, once) and run again.
coach.cmd: guess noted. Run the command, then pick "In the browser" in the scene and run again.

tryNext.ui: Try "My paycheck came in wrong" and "I can’t log into the system". Does the model get the topic without matching words?
tryNext.cmd: Try compare "My paycheck came in wrong" and compare "I can’t log into the system".

why.simples:
An embedding model turns each sentence into a list of numbers that stands for its meaning. Sentences that mean the same thing get similar lists, even with different words.
Word search only finds what’s written the same way.
why.dev:
multilingual-e5-small produces 384-dimension vectors and was trained on about 100 languages. Vectors come out normalized (mean pooling), so cosine similarity becomes a dot product.
E5-family models expect a prefix: "query: " for questions and "passage: " for documents. Forgetting the prefix quietly makes search worse.
why.especialista:
Similarity isn’t truth or business relevance: negated sentences ("I don’t want vacation") sit close to the topic they negate. That’s why semantic search is usually combined with keywords (hybrid) and a reranker.
Pick the model by language and domain, evaluate with your team’s real questions, and version it: switching models means re-embedding the whole index.

phrases: When does this month’s salary come in?
How much is the meal allowance?
Can I work from home on Fridays?
The air conditioning in room 3 is broken

steps: In a Node project or the browser, install @huggingface/transformers.

Run: const e = await pipeline("feature-extraction", "Xenova/multilingual-e5-small"); const v = await e(["query: I want some rest", "query: how do I request vacation?"], { pooling: "mean", normalize: true });
Compute the dot product of the two vectors (v.tolist()).
recipe.ok: the dot product of the two rest/vacation sentences is clearly higher than either one with a password sentence.
